REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - JANUARY 28, 2021 - 07:00 P.M.
ZOOM VIDEO COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID # 829 8657 6141
LEGISLATIVE BODY MEMBERS MAY PARTICIPATE FROM THE CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER, 18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, OR VIA TELECONFERENCE AUTHORIZED BY STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20
* THE CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER REMAINS CLOSED TO THE PUBLIC *
INSTRUCTIONS FOR PUBLIC PARTICIPATION IN THIS MEETING ARE LISTED BELOW
*COVID-19 NOTICE*
To protect public health and safety during the local, state, and federally declared COVID-19 emergency, and in compliance with the current Los Angeles County Health Officer Order, the City Council Chamber remains closed to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-20 this meeting will be conducted via teleconference. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after the distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or by connecting to the ZOOM meeting described below.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting using any of the following methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Teleconference Participation: Live audio public comments can be made by connecting to the meeting using the information listed below. Public speakers will be queued to provide comment at the appropriate time during the meeting agenda and must be available at the time they are called upon to speak.
Cerritos Zoom meeting online link: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82986576141
Cerritos Zoom Meeting call-in telephone number: (669) 900-6833
Cerritos Zoom Meeting ID: 829 8657 6141
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the teleconference meeting.

Items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD JANUARY 28,
2021, 7:00 P.M., IN HYBRID MODE FROM THE COUNCIL CHAMBER, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA AND VIA TELECONFERENCE AS AUTHORIZED BY
STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20, VIA ZOOM VIDEO
COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID# 829 8657 6141

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Naresh Solanki.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Bruce Barrows
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  None.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written correspondence
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Murali Vasudevan submitted written correspondence regarding truck routes and the
  placement and wording of truck route signage.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected
  to speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of January 14,
  2021, 7:00 p.m. (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of January 14, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
 City of Cerritos  January 28, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 7

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7A.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated January 28, 2021
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the Register of
  Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  01/28/2021  $ 4,337,455.24 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of an informational update on the City's response to the
  COVID-19 local emergency (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian & Marketing Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Daisy Legasca inquired as to the date a Cerritos COVID-19 vaccination site may open.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected
  to speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to receive and file the
  informational report (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  January 28, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  Review and consideration of the Cerritos Electric Utility’s (CEU) process, rules and
  regulations for providing electric service to include residential customers (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Ramzi Raufdeen, Electric Utility Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written correspondence
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Gail Grossman submitted written correspondence inquiring about medical discounts and
  level pay programs under the new City service.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected
  to speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Approve the Cerritos Electric Utility process for providing electrical service to
  residential customers in the City of Cerritos; and

  2. Approve the proposed rules and regulations associated with serving electricity to
  residential customers in the City of Cerritos (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING UPDATED POLICIES AND
  PROCEDURES GOVERNING THE CITY’S PARKING PERMIT PROGRAM, AND REPEALING
  RESOLUTION NO. 2015-24 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Daryl Evans, Public Safety Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written correspondence
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Jim McMahon submitted written correspondence regarding the parking permit program
  as it relates to ease of use for senior citizens and support for driveway apron parking.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected
  to speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.
 City of Cerritos  January 28, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 4 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9C.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Waive full reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2021-01, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING UPDATED POLICIES
  AND PROCEDURES GOVERNING THE CITY’S PARKING PERMIT PROGRAM,
  AND REPEALING RESOLUTION NO. 2015-24, inclusive of the following additional
  amendments to the Overnight Parking Policies and Procedures:

  a. 6. SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE PARKING PERMITS

  D. 7.  Other reasons may also necessitate the issuance of a special
  circumstance parking permit. Community Safety Division staff The Public
  Safety Manager will review the merits of each application and render a
  decision that considers the requirements of the resident and community
  at large.

  b. 12. CITY MANAGER APPROVAL OF POLICY

  In my capacity as the Cerritos City Manager, I hereby approve the Policy detailed
  herein for immediate implementation and enforcement.

  This policy was approved by the City Council by way of Resolution No. 2021-01
  on January 28, 2021 and became effective immediately thereon.

  Signed:  Date:

  __________________  _____________
  Mayor

  Signed:  Date:

  __________________  _____________
  City Manager

  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9D.  Review and consideration of an informational budget and audit compliance report for
  Fiscal Year 2020-21 (COUNCIL).

  Staff reports were given by Ryan Carey, Finance Manager, Jeff Thielke, Budget Manager,
  and Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works/Water & Power. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.
 City of Cerritos  January 28, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 5 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9D.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Hu, to receive and file the
  budget and audit compliance report for Fiscal Year 2020-21 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9E.  Review and consideration of the City of Cerritos Comprehensive Annual Financial Report
  for Fiscal Year 2019-20 (COUNCIL).

  Art Gallucci, City Manager, requested the City Council continue this item to the next City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to continue this item to the
  February 11, 2021, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9F.  Review and consideration of the Pine Tree Reforestation Plan – Year One summary
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Todd Kuh, Parks Superintendent. A PowerPoint presentation
  was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written correspondence
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Mark Mackowski submitted written correspondence in support of continuing the tree
  removal project.

  Audio public comments

  Mary Simmons spoke stating the City should be responsible for removal of parkway
  trees and expressed concern as to the continued liability resulting from tree root
  sidewalk damage. She thanked the City Council for their hard work on behalf of the
  residents.
 City of Cerritos  January 28, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 6 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9F.  (continued)

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected
  to speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Continue with the Pine Tree Reforestation Plan; and

  2. Explore the feasibility of:

  a. Installing concrete barriers
  b. Decreasing average costs for pine tree removal
  c. Shifting costs for sidewalk and curb repairs to other funding sources, such as
  Measure M, to focus the General Fund appropriation to pine tree removal,
  exclusively; and

  3. Identify alternative funding for any extra work needed, including sidewalk and gutter
  repair; and

  4. Identify and prioritize the pine trees which are most in need of removal

  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmember Barrows, Mayor Pro Tem Vo, and Mayor
  Solanki.

  CONSENSUS (Vo): Directed the City Manager to partner with the Chamber of
  Commerce regarding the Chamber’s interest in producing the Community Calendar,
  inclusive of such activities as a photography contest for pictures to be included in the
  final product.

  CONSENSUS (Vo): Directed the City Manager to partner with the Chamber of
  Commerce to establish a “medal of valor” program recognizing Cerritos public safety
  members, residents, businesses, City staff, and civilians for extraordinary service to the
  community.
 City of Cerritos  January 28, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 7 of 7

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings
  (continued)

  CONSENSUS (Vo): Directed the City Manager and City Clerk to establish “paperless”
  procedures for public meeting agendas and other regular City processes.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Clerk to explore the feasibility of instituting
  more operationally efficient agenda development/management procedures to support
  further “paperless” processing, inclusive of researching processes utilized by SCAG and
  other surrounding municipalities.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Clerk to place the City Charter Review
  subcommittee’s first report on the February 11, 2021, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor
  Agency agenda.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to prepare an Electronic Devices
  and Services policy and place it on one of the February 2021 Council/Agency meeting
  agendas for City Council review and consideration.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to begin preparations for resuming
  regular Advisory Board meetings.

12.  Closed Session

  None.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 10:52 p.m.

  /s/Vida Barone
  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary
ATTEST:

/s/Naresh Solanki
Naresh Solanki, Mayor/Chair
